source_text: Περὶ τοῦ δεῖν κατὰ τὸν ἐκκλησιαστικὸν κανόνα, τοὺς ἐλευθέρως καὶ νομίμως συναφθέντας δευτέροις γάμοις, μὴ λαθρογαμίαν ποιήσαντας, ὀλίγου χρόνου παρελθόντος, καὶ σχολάσαντας, ταῖς προσευχαῖς καὶ νηστείαις, κατὰ συγγνώμην ἀποδίδοσθαι αὐτοῖς τὴν κοινωνίαν ὡρίσαμεν. Ἐ ρ μ η ν ε ί α. Ο μέν παρών Κανών διορίζει, ότι οι δευτερογαμουντες μετά ολίγον καιρόν να μεταλαμβάνουν τά θεια μυστήρια κατά συγχώρησιν, διά την ανάγκην και πύρωσιν της φύσεως, μόνον εάν ο δεύτερος γάμος αυτων ηναι ελεύθερος και νόμιμος, ητοι δεν είναι εμποδισμένος διά τινα συγγένειαν. Εάν δε κοιμηθουν πρό του να ευλογηθουν, και εάν μετά τον γάμον μετανοήσουν, νηστεύοντες και προσευχόμενοι. Ο δε δ΄. του Βασιλείου ένα χρόνον, η δύω εμποδίζει τους διγάμους από την κοινωνίαν, και φαίνεται ότι εις ολίγον καιρόν συγχωρει η Σύνοδος αυτή τους διγάμους, διά την νηστείαν αυτων και προσευχήν, και απλως ειπειν, διά την αυτων μετάνοιαν• περί ου ανάγνωθι τον ιβ΄ της ά. Ορα και τον ζ΄. της εν Αγκύρα. Εάν δε οι δίγαμοι ουτοι σμίξουν πρό του γάμου, ως πόρνοι επιτιμωνται, κατά τον Ζωναραν, ητοι επτά χρόνους.
thought_title: Second marriages and communion after a short time
orientation: The Council of Laodicea opens with a canon on admitting those who have entered a lawful second marriage to communion after a short period of repentance.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the [necessity] to be necessary according to the ecclesiastical canon, the [ones] freely and lawfully joined together in second marriages, not having made a secret marriage, a little time having passed, and having had leisure, in prayers and fastings, according to concession to be given back to them the communion we defined. Interpretation. The [one] present Canon defines, that the [ones] marrying a second time after a little time to partake of the divine mysteries according to concession, because of the necessity and burning of the nature, only if the second marriage of them is free and lawful, that is [it] is not hindered because of some kinship. If [they] sleep before the [time] to be blessed, and if after the marriage [they] repent, fasting and praying. The [one] fourth of Basil one year, or two hinders the twice-married from the communion, and [it] appears that in a little time [it] concedes this Synod to the twice-married, because of the fasting of them and prayer, and simply to say, because of the repentance of them; concerning which read the twelfth of the first. See also the seventh of the [one] in Ancyra. If the twice-married these have intercourse before the marriage, as fornicators [they] are punished, according to Zonaras, that is seven years.

choices.term: κατὰ συγγνώμην ἀποδίδοσθαι αὐτοῖς τὴν κοινωνίαν
choices.english: by concession the communion is to be given back to them
choices.why: Keeps the passive infinitive with 'to them' as dative of recipient, and 'by concession' for κατὰ συγγνώμην, matching the canonical language of leniency.
rejected: they are to be granted communion by way of pardon
communion is to be restored to them by indulgence

choices.english: not having made a secret marriage
choices.why: Renders the aorist participle with its negative as a condition, preserving the legal nuance that secret unions disqualify.
rejected: not having contracted a clandestine marriage
unless they have not made a secret marriage

choices.english: after a little time has passed
choices.why: Genitive absolute rendered as a temporal clause, keeping the short duration explicit.
rejected: when a short time has elapsed

choices.term: διὰ τὴν ἀνάγκην καὶ πύρωσιν τῆς φύσεως
choices.english: because of the necessity and burning of nature
choices.why: Literal rendering of the explanatory phrase in the interpretation, preserving the physical rationale.
rejected: due to the constraint and heat of nature
on account of natural necessity and passion

choices.term: Εάν δε κοιμηθουν πρό του να ευλογηθουν
choices.english: But if they sleep together before being blessed
choices.why: Keeps the conditional force and the euphemistic verb 'sleep together' for κοιμηθουν, with the passive infinitive 'being blessed' for the marriage blessing.
rejected: But if they have intercourse before the blessing
But if they lie together before being blessed

choices.english: as fornicators they are to be punished
choices.why: Preserves the comparative force of ως and the passive imperative sense of επιτιμωνται.
rejected: they are to be disciplined as fornicators
they are to be censured as fornicators

pass_b_english: Concerning the need, according to the church's canon, that those who have freely and lawfully entered second marriages, and have not made a secret marriage, after a little time has passed and they have devoted themselves to prayers and fasts, are by concession to have communion given back to them—this we decreed.

Interpretation. The present canon determines that those who marry a second time are to partake of the divine mysteries after a little time, by concession, because of the necessity and burning of nature, provided only that their second marriage is free and lawful, that is, not impeded by any kinship. But if they sleep together before being blessed, and if after the marriage they repent, fasting and praying—Basil's fourth canon bars the twice-married from communion for one year or two, and it appears that this synod grants the twice-married communion in a little time because of their fasting and prayer, and simply put, because of their repentance. On this read the twelfth canon of the first synod. See also the seventh canon of the synod at Ancyra. But if these twice-married persons have intercourse before the marriage, they are to be punished as fornicators, according to Zonaras, that is, for seven years.

last_rejected.quote: and have not made a secret marriage
last_rejected.why: μὴ λαθρογαμίαν ποιήσαντας means 'not having committed secret-marriage/bigamy', not 'and have not made a secret marriage'. The Greek is a negative condition they must avoid; English makes it sound like a positive qualification they already met.
last_rejected.ruling: 'And have not made a secret marriage' correctly renders μὴ λαθρογαμίαν ποιήσαντας as a negative participle; no meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: are by concession to have communion given back to them—this we decreed
last_rejected.source_quote: ὀλίγου χρόνου παρελθόντος, καὶ σχολάσαντας, ταῖς προσευχαῖς καὶ νηστείαις, κατὰ συγγνώμην ἀποδίδοσθαι αὐτοῖς τὴν κοινωνίαν ὡρίσαμεν
last_rejected.why: Greek requires time to pass AND devotion to prayers/fasts; English 'after a little time has passed and they have devoted themselves' keeps both, but 'are by concession to have communion given back' loses the temporal conditionality. The main decree is about the process, not automatic restoration.
last_rejected.fix: after a little time has passed and they have given themselves to prayers and fasts, communion is to be restored to them by concession—this we decreed
last_rejected.ruling: English preserves both conditions (time passing, prayers/fasts) and concessional restoration; no real meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: But if they sleep together before being blessed, and if after the marriage they repent, fasting and praying—Basil's fourth canon bars the twice-married from communion for one year or two
last_rejected.source_quote: Εάν δε κοιμηθουν πρό του να ευλογηθουν, και εάν μετά τον γάμον μετανοήσουν, νηστεύοντες και προσευχόμενοι. Ο δε δ΄. του Βασιλείου ένα χρόνον, η δύω εμποδίζει τους διγάμους από την κοινωνίαν
last_rejected.why: The dash makes Basil’s one- or two-year bar the result of sleeping together before the blessing. In the source that bar is a separate statement about the twice-married.
last_rejected.fix: But if they sleep together before being blessed, and if after the marriage they repent, fasting and praying. Basil’s fourth canon bars the twice-married from communion for one year or two.
last_rejected.ruling: The source has a fragment ('Εάν δε κοιμηθουν… μετανοήσουν') followed by a separate sentence 'Ο δε δ΄. του Βασιλείου…'. The English dash keeps that order and doesn't make Basil's bar a result.
